Dryness: Moisture lives in water: refresh with a water-based leave-in mid-week, then seal (LOC).
Breakage: Most breakage is mechanical: detangle only when wet and conditioned, and cut back on daily combing.
Split ends: Splits can’t be glued back. Trim every 12 weeks and you’ll keep more length, not less.
Tangles and knots: Single-strand knots form on ends: detangle in sections and stretch hair (braids or twists) to sleep.
Thin edges: Usually tension: skip tight ponytails, edge brushing and heavy wigs glued at the hairline. If they don’t recover in 6 months, see a dermatologist; long-standing traction loss can be permanent.
Shrinkage: Shrinkage is a sign of healthy coils. Stretch with banding or twist-outs, not heat.
Dandruff or itchy scalp: Flakes plus itch is usually a yeast: a ketoconazole or zinc pyrithione shampoo 1 to 2 times a week works better than oils, which can feed it.
Frizz: Apply stylers to soaking-wet hair and let it dry without touching.
